verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same five rows for the same reference pair U₀ = 4η, E₀ = P∗ f x^{1/10}: `manuscriptIdealRows` is exactly the vector (M̂₀, Î₀, Ĵ₀, Ŝ₀, C_{p,0}) and `ideal_rows_moments` states that it equals the moments of that pair, with `dilationFactor = ![R, R√R, R√R, R, 1]` supplying the paper's hat normalisation. The rewriting is the evaluation of three elementary integrals: ∫₀^x √(2t) t^{1/10} dt = (5√2/8) x^{8/5} (Lean keeps this as `idealWeightI` and proves only the bound `idealWeightI_bound : |idealWeightI r| ≤ 2r`), ∫₀^x t^{1/5}/2 dt = (5/12) x^{6/5} (`idealWeightS`, again only bounded, `≤ r/2`), and ∫₀^x t^{1/5}/(2t) dt = (5/2) x^{1/5}, which Lean does evaluate in closed form in `idealWeightP_eq`, matching C_{p,0} exactly. So the paper's explicit powers for Î₀ and Ŝ₀ are not written out as a Lean equation; they follow by the same ∫ t^a computation the repository already performs for the pressure row, and their x = 1 values do appear verbatim as `OutgoingHistories.initialS` (16η² − (5/12)P²f²) and `OutgoingSchedule.angularMoment` (leading term (5/2)√2 P η f = Ĵ₀(1)).
